Growth chart with reference curves and a child's measurements

Source: R/desc-plots.R
wgh_plot_growth_chart.Rd

Draws reference curves for one sex and indicator, either as percentile curves (3rd, 15th, 50th, 85th and 97th by default) or as standard deviation (z-score) curves (-3 to +3 SD by default), and overlays the measurements of one or more children. The reference can be the WHO standards and reference (default), the CDC 2000 growth charts, or your own LMS table. Generalises plot_growth_chart() from Book 1 Chapter 5.

Usage

wgh_plot_growth_chart(
  x = NULL,
  ids = NULL,
  indicator = c("hfa", "wfa", "bfa"),
  sex = NULL,
  lines = c("percentile", "sd"),
  centiles = c(3, 15, 50, 85, 97),
  sd_lines = -3:3,
  reference = "who",
  age_range = c(2, 18),
  band = FALSE,
  label_lines = TRUE,
  line_colour = NULL,
  child_colour = "grey15",
  ...
)

Arguments

x

Data with id (or pid), age, sex and the measurement.

ids

Children to plot. When NULL, only the reference is drawn.

indicator

"hfa" (height), "wfa" (weight) or "bfa" (BMI).

sex

Sex of the chart (taken from the first child when NULL).

lines

"percentile" or "sd".

centiles

Percentiles to draw when lines = "percentile".

sd_lines

Z-scores to draw when lines = "sd".

reference

"who", "cdc" or a custom LMS table (see wgh_reference()).

age_range

Age range in years (default 2 to 18).

band

Shade the area between the outermost curves.

label_lines

Label each curve at its right end.

line_colour

Colour of the reference curves (default by sex).

child_colour

Colour of the child's measurements. With several children, use NULL to colour each child differently.

...

Display options (see wgh_plot_options()), for example title, base_size or y_limits.

Value

A ggplot object.

Next steps

Read a child's z-scores with wgh_add_zscores(), compare references with wgh_compare_references(), or build a personalised expected range with wgh_condref() and wgh_plot_fan().

Examples

girl <- growdat$pid[growdat$sex == "Female"][1]
# WHO percentiles (default)
wgh_plot_growth_chart(growdat, ids = girl)

# WHO standard deviation curves
wgh_plot_growth_chart(growdat, ids = girl, lines = "sd")

# CDC 2000 percentiles for BMI, with a shaded band and a custom title
wgh_plot_growth_chart(growdat, ids = girl, indicator = "bfa", reference = "cdc",
                      centiles = c(5, 50, 85, 95), band = TRUE, title = "BMI-for-age, CDC 2000")

# Reference curves only, for boys
wgh_plot_growth_chart(sex = "Male", lines = "sd", sd_lines = c(-2, 0, 2))
